:::{#thm-de-morgan}
#### De Morgan's law for a union

Let $S$ be a set, let $I$ be a nonempty set of indices,
and let $A_i$ be a [subset](#def-subset) of $S$ for each $i \in I$.
Then the complement of a union is the intersection of the complements
[@wikipedia_de_morgans_laws]:

$$
S \setminus \bigcup_{i \in I} A_i = \bigcap_{i \in I} (S \setminus A_i)
$$

With the complement notation of @def-complement,
this reads $\paren{\bigcup_{i \in I} A_i}^c = \bigcap_{i \in I} A_i^c$.

:::

::: proof

Two sets are equal when they have the same elements (@def-set),
so it is enough to show that an element $x$ is in the left-hand side
[if and only if](proof-writing.qmd#def-necessary-sufficient) ($\iff$)
it is in the right-hand side.
Each step applies the definition named at its right:
set difference (@def-set-difference), union (@def-union) or intersection (@def-intersection).

$$
\ba
x \in S \setminus \bigcup_{i \in I} A_i
&\iff x \in S \text{ and } x \notin \bigcup_{i \in I} A_i
&& \text{(set difference)} \\
&\iff x \in S \text{ and } x \notin A_i \text{ for every } i \in I
&& \text{(union)} \\
&\iff x \in S \setminus A_i \text{ for every } i \in I
&& \text{(set difference)} \\
&\iff x \in \bigcap_{i \in I} (S \setminus A_i)
&& \text{(intersection)}
\ea
$$

:::
